target_customer: TV networks and advertisers (analytics, after pivot); consumers (Moki.TV directory, before pivot)
problem: TV and streaming viewers could not easily find where content was available; after the pivot the problem was measuring real-time social conversation around TV.
business_model: Undetermined; no revenue disclosed. Analytics product was acquired for the team.
product_category: Social TV analytics (originally a streaming content directory)

competitors.name: Bluefin Labs
competitors.what: Social TV analytics linking audience comments to shows

competitors.name: SocialGuide
competitors.what: Social TV comment tracking, in beta for movies
competitors.traction_then: smaller comment flow than Bluefin per Xconomy

technical_complexity.rationale: Real-time ingestion and analysis of social streams at small team scale; the Moki.TV directory required aggregating catalogs across streaming services.

defensibility.rationale: Better funded rivals were already selling TV analytics and Twitter owned the data firehose.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Twitter acquired the Hotspots team in April 2012 for its revenue engineering group and later bought Bluefin Labs.

market_need_then: Brands and networks were beginning to pay for social TV measurement in 2011 and 2012, as the coverage of Bluefin Labs and SocialGuide shows.

branding.domain_note: YC page lists moki.tv; the later product used hotspots.io; no purchase history found.

rebrands.why: Pivot from content directory to social analytics; reason not stated by a source

brand_strength.rationale: Little press about the brand beyond acquisition coverage; the name is generic and collides with wifi hotspot results.

pivots.from: Moki.TV, a directory of paid and free streaming content
pivots.to: Hotspots.io, real-time social analytics for TV
pivots.why: Not stated in sources; date approximate

outcome_analysis: Hotspots began as Moki.TV, a directory of streaming content, and pivoted to social TV analytics, a space where Bluefin Labs and SocialGuide already operated. Twitter acquired the team in April 2012 for its revenue engineering group; CB Insights labels it an acquisition of talent and no price was disclosed. With no disclosed funding or revenue it reads as an acquihire exit rather than a scaled business.
notes: moki.tv returned HTTP 522 on fetch, treated as a dead or unreachable site. Press names a third team member, Ashutosh Singhal, but the YC page lists only two founders so he is not listed. Funding search found nothing; none_found does not mean no funding. The acquihire label is from CB Insights per a search summary. Competitor source articles are dated November 2011; both firms were operating by then, and the as_of is set within six months of the batch.
